keyVerseText: Our cattle also shall go with us; there shall not an hoof be left behind; for thereof must we take to serve the LORD our God; and we know not with what we must serve the LORD, until we come thither.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun פַּרְסָה (parçâh) is etymologically connected as the feminine form of פֶּרֶס (pereç), which primarily denotes a claw or a bird of prey such as an ossifrage. This root suggests an original sense related to a sharp, divided extremity used for grasping or support. Thus, beyond the common English gloss of 'hoof,' the root meaning conveys not just a simple foot covering but a functional, divided appendage essential for movement and stability in animals.
usageInScripture: The word פַּרְסָה appears 21 times in the Hebrew Bible and is predominantly translated as 'hoof' or 'the hoof,' particularly referring to the feet of ruminants and horses. The usage includes both literal references to animal hooves and figurative applications, such as in prophetic imagery. The range of translations—from 'claws' to 'hoof' and 'hoofs'—reflects the word's flexibility in describing various types of foot structures, including split hooves of ruminants and undivided hooves of horses, indicating a broad semantic field centered on animal extremities.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding פַּרְסָה as a term rooted in the anatomy of animal feet enriches our grasp of biblical purity laws and sacrificial practices, where distinctions between cloven and uncloven hooves carry covenantal significance. This word reminds believers of God's design in creation, emphasizing order and holiness even in the natural world. The precise language used to describe animal features underscores the seriousness with which God approaches holiness and separation. For the Christian faith, this highlights the importance of obedience to God's commands and the recognition that all creation is under His sovereign care and purpose.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 10:26 declares, 'Our cattle also shall go with us; there shall not an hoof be left behind,' emphasizing the completeness of the judgment on Egypt's livestock during the plague. The use of פַּרְסָה here stresses that not even the smallest part of the animals' feet will be spared, symbolizing totality in God's judgment and provision. This word deepens the verse's impact by focusing on the thoroughness of God's actions and the seriousness of His covenant relationship with His people, who must bring their best to serve the LORD.
